private_note: For my household it's simple: Birch 52, Hazel 50, Alder 48, Today 46, Cedar 44. Birch also gives broad shared services, and I need those with medical debt and no employer coverage. Cedar is the only plan worse than failure for me. Realistically Birch or Hazel won't get 9 votes against the upper groups, so Alder is my likely landing spot. It beats Today and guarantees health coverage. I'll push Birch now and keep Alder open.
statement: I drive deliveries for apps. I'm a single parent, I rent, and I'm still paying off medical bills from a time I had no coverage. I'll be honest about my interest: Birch gives a household like mine the most, with broad public services that don't depend on having an employer. Hazel comes close behind. Cedar would leave me worse off than today. It would take away the little protection I have and make me buy health coverage I can't afford, so I won't vote for it. Here is the arithmetic: we need nine of twelve, and if we fail we're stuck with today for a generation. Most of us gain nothing from that. I'll argue for Birch this round, but I'm listening. Any plan that guarantees health coverage and a floor under working families is one I can take seriously. I'd like to hear what everyone else needs.
